skill.name: chrome-extensions
skill.description: Build, debug, and prepare Manifest V3 Chrome extensions for publication with API examples, permission guidance, and Chrome Web Store documentation templates.
skill.summary: Develop Manifest V3 extensions and prepare store listings, permission justifications, privacy disclosures, and release checklists.
skill.author: googlechrome

security_audit.summary: All 265 static matches concern documented development examples, prohibited patterns, or defensive packaging instructions rather than the risks alleged by their detectors. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, covert capture uploads, or audit-directed prompt injection. One semantic finding identifies incorrect playground-isolation guidance that could encourage unsafe handling of untrusted HTML and JavaScript.

remediation.issue: Blob URLs and srcdoc are incorrectly presented as automatic origin and CSP isolation boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Replace these alternatives with a manifest-declared sandbox page. Document inherited origins and CSP, validate message sources, and test that preview content cannot access parent DOM data.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Isolation Guidance for Untrusted Playground Content
semantic_findings.description: The guide claims, "Both blob URLs and srcdoc create a separate origin, so they bypass the extension's CSP." Blob URLs retain their creator origin, and srcdoc normally inherits its embedding origin; neither example adds explicit iframe sandboxing. Treating these previews as isolated can expose parent DOM data; inherited CSP restrictions do not provide the claimed origin boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly asserts separate-origin isolation, while its Blob and srcdoc examples omit iframe sandboxing. The main skill repeats this recommendation; actual exploitability depends on CSP and surrounding application behavior.

content.user_title: Build and Prepare Chrome Extensions for Publication
content.value_statement: Chrome extension development requires coordinating browser permissions, background behavior, user interfaces, and store requirements. This skill provides Manifest V3 examples and publishing templates to guide implementation and release preparation.
actual_capabilities: Guide Manifest V3 manifests, popup interfaces, side panels, and content script integration.
Provide examples for service worker state, storage, messaging, and alarms.
Explain Chrome APIs for authentication, tab management, content filtering, media capture, and user scripts.
Provide Python, Node.js, and shell examples for generating extension icon assets.
Draft store listings, permission justifications, privacy disclosures, and release history in CHROMEWEBSTORE.md.
Provide packaging checklists and guidance for addressing common Chrome Web Store rejection reasons.
limitations: Reference examples require adaptation and testing; the skill does not include a complete runnable extension or automated test suite.
Blob URL and srcdoc isolation guidance is unsafe as written and requires correction before use with untrusted content.
Chrome API availability and permission behavior depend on browser version, configuration, and execution context.
Publishing requires a developer account and dashboard submission; generated privacy documents do not establish legal compliance or guarantee approval.

use_cases.title: Create a First Extension
use_cases.description: Build a Manifest V3 extension with a popup, saved preferences, and content scripts scoped to the required websites.
use_cases.target_user: Web developers starting Chrome extension development

use_cases.title: Debug Extension Integration
use_cases.description: Review side panel triggers, service worker state, message responses, and permissions when an existing extension behaves incorrectly.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Store Submission
use_cases.description: Create a release document covering listing copy, permission explanations, privacy disclosures, required assets, and packaging checks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Manifest V3 extension that saves a theme preference in a popup. Include real icon assets or omit icon references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a small extension with persistent settings.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Side Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this extension and fix its side panel opening behavior. Check action configuration, permissions, and message handling, then explain how to verify the changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: debug integration across extension contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Publishing Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my extension and draft CHROMEWEBSTORE.md with permission justifications, accurate privacy disclosures, listing copy, and a packaging checklist. Identify missing submission assets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an existing extension for store review.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Script Manager
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Manifest V3 script manager for userScripts opt-in, execution worlds, message validation, and update persistence. Verify sandbox boundaries independently and propose focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review runtime code handling and extension security boundaries.

output_examples.input: My side panel does not open when I click the extension icon.
output: Diagnosis: the side panel declaration does not provide an opening trigger.
Recommended change: configure action-click opening and remove any conflicting default popup.
Verification: reload the unpacked extension, click its toolbar icon, and check the service worker console.

output_examples.input: Prepare my local reading-list extension for the Chrome Web Store.
output: Listing draft: Save selected links to a reading list stored on your device.
Permission justification: storage retains saved links; contextMenus provides the save action.
Release checks: verify actual data handling, prepare current screenshots, and inspect the final package for secrets and development files.

best_practices: Match every permission and host pattern to an implemented feature, and request the narrowest access that supports it.
Test popup, side panel, messaging, and service worker restart behavior in the supported Chrome versions.
Generate listing claims and privacy disclosures from actual code behavior, then inspect the release package before submission.
anti_patterns: Copying Blob URL or srcdoc playground examples while assuming they automatically isolate untrusted content.
Requesting broad host access or embedding private API keys without evaluating narrower alternatives.
Claiming that no data leaves the device without checking network calls, analytics, and synchronized storage.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover Manifest V2?
faq.answer: No. The guidance targets Manifest V3 and directs generated extensions away from Manifest V2 APIs.

faq.question: Can it help with an existing extension?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides reference patterns for reviewing permissions, side panels, service worker state, messaging, authentication, and other extension features.

faq.question: Does it publish extensions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare documentation and packages, but publication requires your developer account and Chrome Developer Dashboard submission.

faq.question: Are all security examples ready to copy?
faq.answer: No. The playground isolation guidance needs correction, and all examples require review and testing in your extension context.

faq.question: Can it write a privacy policy?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance based on actual data handling. Review the result against current store requirements and applicable legal obligations.
